1. Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for
petitioner.
2. Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned counsel holding brief
of Mrs. Bina Pande, learned counsel for respondent
no.1.
3. Petitioner was appointed as Assistant Manager
(Legal) in University of Petroleum and Energy Studies,
Dehradun on 16.07.2015. His services were
terminated vide order dated 19.04.2016. I n this Writ
Petition, petitioner has challenged his termination by
the said order.
4. I t is contended by learned counsel for petitioner
that since petitioner's services were confirmed vide
order dated 04.01.2016, therefore, he could not have
been terminated, without holding regular disciplinary
enquiry. I t is further contended that the impugned
termination order does not indicate any reason for
termination of petitioner's services.
5. Per contra, Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned counsel
holding brief of Mrs. Bina Pande, learned counsel for
University of Petroleum and Energy Studies subm its
that this Writ Petition is not maintainable, as University
of Petroleum and Energy Studies is neither getting any
financial aid from the Government - Central or State,
nor the Government is exercising adm inistrative control
over its affairs. A statement to this effect is made in
paragraph no. 5 of the counter affidavit of respondent

2024:UHC:8995-DB
no. 1, which is extracted below:
"5. That the Respondent is not a state aided university
and therefore is not a state within the m eaning of Article
12 of the Constitution of I ndia and therefore in light of this
sole ground the present Petition is not m aintainable and is
liable to be dism issed."
6. No rejoinder affidavit has been filed by petitioner.
Thus, the averment made in paragraph no. 5 of the
counter affidavit of respondent no. 1 remains
uncontroverted.
7. Law is well settled that a body, which is under
direct adm inistrative and financial control of the State
alone, can be treated as a State under Article 12 of the
Constitution of I ndia. There is no dispute that
University of Petroleum and Energy Studies is a private
University, which is neither getting any aid from the
Government - Central or State, nor the State or
Central Government is exercising administrative
control over its affairs. Therefore, in view of the law
laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
Pr ad eep Ku m ar Bisw as v . I n d ian I n st it u t e of
Ch em ical Biolog y an d Or s., ( 2 0 0 2 ) 5 SCC 1 1 1 , we
are of the opinion that this Writ Petition would not be
maintainable.
8. Accordingly, the present Writ Petition is
dism issed as not m aintainable, with liberty to petitioner
to approach the appropriate forum
9. Pending application(s), if any, also stand
disposed of.

( Viv ek Bh ar t i Sh ar m a, J.) ( Man o j Ku m ar Tiw ar i, A.C.J.)
